instruction: Extract the 'Low-Carbon Development' section from GE Guidebook.pdf on the Desktop and compile it into a Google Doc titled 'lowcarbon_development_summary' in the /climate_action folder for the climate action committee meeting.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the 'Low-Carbon Development' section from GE Guidebook.pdf and creating a Google Doc named 'lowcarbon_development_summary' in the /climate_action folder. The evaluator checks for key low-carbon development concepts (climate change, emissions, development) with minimum length requirement. Custom getter extracts document text, metric validates keyword presence with partial credit scoring.

scoring_breakdown.0.7: Contains all required keywords (low-carbon, climate change, emissions, development)
scoring_breakdown.1.0: Title keywords appear in first 500 characters

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads and extracts text from Google Doc at specified path ['climate_action', 'lowcarbon_development_summary']
Metric appropriately validates content relevance using keyword checking for 'low-carbon', 'climate change', 'emissions', 'development'
Partial credit scoring logic is well-designed: 0.4 for document existence, +0.3 for keyword coverage, +0.2 for length, +0.1 for title keywords
Document location verification is correct - getter config specifies the right path matching instruction requirements
Title keyword check in first 500 characters helps verify content is on-topic about Low-Carbon Development
Minimum length requirement (700 chars) ensures substantive content extraction, not just copying a few sentences
Empty document handling is correct - getter returns empty string if file missing, metric returns 0.0 for empty content
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor limitation: Evaluator cannot verify that content was actually extracted from GE Guidebook.pdf vs. being created from other sources, but this is practically difficult to verify without source comparison

Consider: The instruction says 'extract content about Low-Carbon Development' which implies specific section extraction, but the evaluator only checks for keyword presence. This is a reasonable approximation given the difficulty of verifying exact extraction fidelity
